title: Basic, predefined and custom roles: which one to reach for

videos.script: A permission is one thing an API lets you do. Publish to a topic. Delete a project. {{permission}} A role is a set of permissions with a name. And only a role can be granted, never a permission on its own. {{role}} So every grant joins three things. Who. Which role. And on what. {{grant}} The first roles anybody meets are the three basic ones. Viewer, Editor and Owner. They are too big for almost every job. {{basic}} Editor can delete the database while it deploys the website. Owner can grant itself anything at all. {{big}} Predefined roles are sized for one job in one service. Viewer, a few working roles, editor, admin. The same ladder, everywhere. {{ladder}} And when nothing fits, you write a custom role. In your lab, the provider refuses its first name. Then it plans the role, and a grant of it. {{custom}} A custom role is yours to maintain. It never grows on its own. {{end}}
